body: The release decision for frontier AI systems increasingly relies on cyber capability benchmarks, yet public vulnerability benchmarks can expose agents to previously published advisories, exploits, and fixes, making it difficult to distinguish prior exposure from capability on unseen vulnerabilities. We evaluate open-weight and proprietary AI models on exploit generation, vulnerability repair and subsequent attacks in five nonpublic software environments, including vulnerabilities we privately disclosed while they remained unpatched. Researcher-developed and reviewed deterministic graders, not LLM judges, determine task scores. Comparisons with 209 disclosed vulnerabilities and cryptographic challenges reveal substantial variation across systems and vulnerability types. Repair scores exceed attack scores in two nonpublic environments and fall below them in three. Passing an initial security test is also insufficient: another exploit succeeds in 92 of 524 non-independent defender test intervals after the initial exploit is stopped. These results motivate vulnerability-specific attack-repair comparisons and subsequent resistance tests.
summaryZh: 本文通过在五个非公开软件环境中评估大模型的漏洞利用与修复能力，探讨了AI在网络安全中的双重角色。研究采用了研究人员开发的确定性评分器而非LLM判别器，确保了评估的客观性。实验发现，模型在漏洞修复与攻击生成方面的表现存在显著差异，且通过初步安全测试并不意味着具备长期的防御韧性。该研究强调了针对特定漏洞进行攻击-修复对比测试的必要性，为评估前沿AI系统的网络安全能力提供了严谨的方法论。

指利用软件漏洞编写攻击代码或脚本的过程。
